title: Disjunction and witnesses in equality-free intuitionistic first-order logic

based_on.title: Proof Theory 2018: Sequent calculus for predicate logic (handout 9)
Proofs and Types (web reprint 2003, corrected 1990 edition)

summary: Read actual disjunct and witness data from pure first-order proofs, preserving original names or the explicitly visible auxiliary reserve.
abstract: Proving that something exists is especially informative when the proof supplies a term that works. For pure equality-free intuitionistic logic, removing logical cuts exposes such a term together with a proof of its instance, while a theorem disjunction exposes a chosen disjunct. These data come from the final inference of an assumption-free proof. Temporary parameters remain visible in the extracted terms: they can be removed when an original term is supplied, but a constant-free language may have none. The empty-assumption condition also matters, since an assumed existential statement need not select any original-name witness.
